Compare SSE-S3, SSE-KMS, SSE-C and client-side encryption.

SSE-S3: key managed by S3, AES-256, enabled by default. SSE-KMS: key in KMS, control and CloudTrail audit, but KMS quotas. SSE-C: key supplied by the customer with every HTTPS request, S3 does not store it. Client-side: the client encrypts before sending and the server can never decrypt. I choose based on who must control and audit the key.
How do you enforce HTTPS and SSE-KMS on a bucket?

With Deny bucket policies: one denies s3:* when aws:SecureTransport is false; the other denies s3:PutObject when s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption is not aws:kms. Bucket policies are evaluated before default encryption. For large files with KMS, the caller needs kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt, and the Bucket Key reduces KMS calls by up to 99%.
What is the difference between Governance and Compliance, and between Vault Lock and Object Lock?

Object Lock protects S3 object versions (versioning required); in Compliance mode, even root can neither delete nor shorten the retention, while in Governance mode some privileged users can bypass it. Legal hold is independent of the duration. Vault Lock irreversibly locks a Glacier vault policy after a 24-hour process with a Lock ID.
